f.title: State pharmacovigilance contact point in the letter of undertaking
f.statement: The NDA must include a letter of undertaking signed by the applicant agreeing to provide, at any stage of registration, any information and/or documents relating to the product upon request within the prescribed timeframe; the contact details of both the regulatory and pharmacovigilance contact points should be stated.
f.applicability: New drug applications (NDA-1, NDA-2, NDA-3) for initial registration in Hong Kong

f.title: Provide locally reported serious ADRs from local clinical trials with the NDA
f.statement: The NDA should include information on pre-registration importation of the product in Hong Kong; if a clinical trial has been or will be conducted locally, information including the clinical trial certificate number, trial site, principal investigator and locally reported serious adverse drug reactions should be provided.
f.applicability: New drug applications (NDA-1, NDA-2, NDA-3) for initial registration in Hong Kong

f.title: Submit a proposed RMP and/or REMS for implementation in Hong Kong
f.statement: The NDA should include a proposed Risk Management Plan (RMP) and/or Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) to be implemented in Hong Kong, taking into account the identified and potential risks and missing information of the product. For NDAs via the abridged evaluation and verification routes, the proposed RMP/REMS should take reference to that currently approved by the regulatory authorities of the listed reference countries/places.

f.title: During NDA review, report foreign regulatory actions within 72 hours
f.statement: After submission of an NDA and during the application process, the applicant is required to report any regulatory actions taken by health authorities outside Hong Kong, including but not limited to withdrawal or refusal of applications, suspension or revocation of marketing authorisations or distribution, clinical holds, safety alerts, restriction of indications and product recalls, within 72 hours.

f.title: After registration, report all serious ADRs occurring in Hong Kong
f.statement: Upon registration, the applicant is required to report all serious adverse drug reactions of the product occurring in Hong Kong, any actions taken by health authorities outside Hong Kong, any changes of the manufacturer or manufacturing process and any product recalls to the Drug Office within a prescribed time frame.

f.statement: For NDAs via the primary or abridged evaluation routes, the applicant will also be required to report all unexpected adverse drug reactions of the product occurring in Hong Kong, and any actions taken by health authorities outside Hong Kong, including withdrawal or refusal of applications.

f.title: Keep the Hong Kong RMP updated (global RMP changes; Committee requests; risk system changes)
f.statement: For NDAs via the abridged evaluation route, the applicant will be required to update the proposed RMP in accordance with the global RMP when the latter is modified and implemented in the relevant countries/places. For NDAs via the primary evaluation route, the applicant will be required to update the RMP at the request of the Committee or whenever the risk management system is modified, especially as the result of new information that may lead to a significant change to the benefit/risk profile or of an important (pharmacovigilance or risk minimisation) milestone being reached.

f.statement: Upon registration, the applicant is required to submit all final reports of all planned, on-going or future clinical studies of the product for reassessment at the same time as they are submitted to the relevant drug regulatory authorities, with a summary of the conclusion of the studies and the proposed follow-up actions.

f.title: Inform the Drug Office of foreign regulatory actions arising from study results within 72 hours
f.statement: The applicant must inform the Drug Office of any regulatory actions taken by the relevant drug regulatory authorities in view of the results of the clinical studies of the product as soon as possible, and in any event no later than 72 hours after the actions have been taken.

f.title: Submit PBRERs 6-monthly for 2 years, then annually for 3 years
